NEVER git commit, never touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, never run `uv`, NEVER call a model (not `claude`, not `codex`), NEVER use the network, never run `python -m bench run`, never write factory/state/. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv . Environment for every command: `export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp`. Ruff (python files only): `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` / `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` (line length 120, Python 3.12). Never pass --cov to pytest. Run tests as `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 <files>`. Tests must be hermetic (fake runner, no network, no real `claude`). Shared code must stay story-agnostic (no story, scene or character names in production code). If an OLD test pins behaviour this change deliberately changes, update it and say so in NOTES.txt. Write NOTES.txt (worktree root, never committed) listing every ambiguity and your choice. Read first: AGENTS.md and docs/contributor-guide.md. You may edit ONLY: storygame/runtime/pacing_replay.py (new), tests/test_pacing_replay.py (new) and tests/shard_durations.json (one entry for the new test file, same format as its neighbours, value 2.0). You may READ storygame/runtime/engine.py but must NOT edit it. Nothing else.

BACKGROUND. The outcome contract (tests/fixtures/outcome_contract/README.md, read it; and .plans/qualification/null-grounding-decision.md section 'Contract wording') must tell a reveal the player earned from one the clock caused. Decision (owner, 2026-11-23): PACING-ONLY REPLAY. Before a turn's pacing pass, replay only that pass on a COPY of the pre-command state: the same turn advance and none of the command's effects. Every PACING EVENT (`package.pacing.events`) that fires in the replay is a pressure event; the knowledge it makes deliverable is the union of those events' `delivers` lists (a tuple of knowledge ids on PacingEvent, added in round 29a) and becomes `null_grounding_ids`. Storylets the clock merely opens (`package.storylet_routes.storylets`) are NEVER null grounding. A pacing event that fires only because the command changed a fact will not fire in the replay (its `when` is false on the pre-command facts), so it is the world answering the player and stays progress. No model call is made.

WHAT A TURN DOES (read RuntimeEngine in storygame/runtime/engine.py): `turn_index += 1`, then the pre-narration `_activate_pacing(realize_complications=True, defer_guarded_events=True)` (it skips trailing events and events whose `when` holds an `equals is False` predicate), then the provider narrates, then the post-commit lifecycle runs `_activate_pacing(realize_complications=True)` again. The replay copies only that pacing work: on a scratch copy advance `turn_index` by one, run the pre-narration pass, then the post-commit pass (the same `_activate_pacing` code, so the rule is not re-implemented), and report which `package.pacing.events` ids newly entered `fired_event_ids`.

BUILD storygame/runtime/pacing_replay.py: a frozen dataclass or pydantic model `PacingReplay` with `fired_event_ids: tuple[str, ...]` (package order) and `null_grounding_ids: tuple[str, ...]` (union of `delivers` of the fired events, package order, no duplicates), and one public function `replay_pacing(engine) -> PacingReplay`. HARD REQUIREMENTS: it must not change the live engine in any way (state, facts, fired and active event ids, last_turn_delivery, staged cue and handoff fields, turn records, attempts, provider, capture, projector), must not call the provider or the capture, and must be deterministic. A transition-firing pacing event calls `apply_proposal` on the scratch state; that must not escape either. Copy with the pattern storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py already uses (look at lines near 109-124) or `copy.deepcopy` of the state with the story package shared through the `memo` argument (the package is immutable and large; never deep-copy it), or build a scratch `RuntimeState` from `state.snapshot()`; choose what is simplest and proven by your tests, and state it in NOTES.txt. Story-agnostic code only (no story, scene, character or claim names in production code). Say in NOTES.txt why this is a runtime adapter and not a `World` method in packages/worldkeeper (it reads package pacing events, not only world state).

TESTS, WRITE THEM FIRST in tests/test_pacing_replay.py (hermetic: no network, no model, no real provider; follow how tests/test_trailing_pacing_events.py builds a RuntimeEngine with a fake provider and how it loads `data/stories/continuity-initiative`; you may also use `compiled_story_copy` and `patch_source` from tests/story_source/helpers.py; read both first): (1) NO SIDE EFFECTS: build an engine in a scene one turn before a pacing event's `at_turn`, take `state.snapshot()` (and a dump of every field the replay might touch), call `replay_pacing`, and assert the snapshot and those fields are unchanged and the provider was called zero times; (2) FIRES ON TIME: in the real package scene 2A with `turns_since_entry` one below the `at_turn` of event `inspection_window_2a` and its `when` satisfied, the replay's `fired_event_ids` contains that id; one turn earlier it does not; (3) DELIVERS: on a package copy where that event has `delivers=('k_inspection_window_missed',)` (derive with pydantic `model_copy(update=...)` on the frozen models, or patch the source copy), `null_grounding_ids` equals ('k_inspection_window_missed',); with no `delivers` it is empty while `fired_event_ids` still lists the event; (4) CLOCK-OPENED STORYLETS ARE NOT NULL GROUNDING: at a state where a storylet is clock-open, no storylet id or storylet knowledge id appears in either field; (5) THE COMMAND'S OWN FACT: pick or build (by patching the source copy) a pacing event whose `when` needs a fact that is false before the command; in the replay it is absent; after you assert that fact on the live state it is present; (6) PARITY: play one real turn with the fake provider on a fresh engine and compare: every `package.pacing.events` id that newly fired during the real turn on a no-effect command equals the replay's `fired_event_ids` computed just before that turn (run the replay on an identical second engine so the first stays untouched); (7) TRANSITION EVENT: if a pacing event with a `transition_id` exists, the replay reports it without moving the live scene. If none can be reached cheaply, skip nothing silently: say so in NOTES.txt and add a package-copy test with such an event. (8) calling twice returns equal results.
Run the tests; also run tests/test_trailing_pacing_events.py and tests/test_engine*.py to confirm nothing else moved (you edit no existing file).
tasks.check:
set -eo pipefail
WORK=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-29c
mkdir -p "$WORK/out"
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
git reset -q
git add -A -- storygame tests
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=d | grep -vE '^(storygame/runtime/pacing_replay\.py|tests/test_pacing_replay\.py|tests/shard_durations\.json)$' || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
start=$(date +%s)
out=$(.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs -n 4 tests/test_pacing_replay.py tests/test_trailing_pacing_events.py 2>&1) || { echo "$out"; exit 1; }
echo "$out" | tail -6
took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))
echo "tests took $took s (budget 240 s)"
[ "$took" -le 240 ] || { echo "over the 240 s budget"; exit 1; }
case "$out" in *skipped*) echo "tests were skipped"; exit 1;; esac
grep -q '"tests/test_pacing_replay.py"' tests/shard_durations.json || { echo "tests/shard_durations.json lacks the new test file"; exit 1; }
.venv/bin/python -m json.tool tests/shard_durations.json > /dev/null
grep -nE "k_sl_|k_scene_|k_bridge|SL-[0-9]|\b[123][A-C]\b|inspection|kristin" storygame/runtime/pacing_replay.py && { echo "story-specific names in production code"; exit 1; } || true
git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q "storygame/runtime/engine.py" && { echo "engine.py must not change"; exit 1; } || true
PYFILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=d | grep '\.py$' || true)
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff check $PYFILES
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check $PYFILES
git diff --cached > "$WORK/out/pacing-replay.patch"
test -s "$WORK/out/pacing-replay.patch"
